questions.question: -40 degrees Fahrenheit is equal to how many degrees on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**– 40.**__

__
 
• **-40 degrees**__ is the temperature that shows the **same measurement **in Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.
 
• On a Fahrenheit scale, the intervals between the ice point and the steam point are divided into **180 equal parts.**
 
• The following mathematical equation is used to convert the Fahrenheit scale(F) to Celsius scale(C):
 __
 
• C=(F -32)times {5over9}
 
 
 
• Given that;
 
 
• F= -40.
 
• Substitute the value of F in the above equation:
 
• C=(-40 -32)times {5over9}
 
• C=(-72)times {5over9}
 
• C= -40.
 
 
 
• -40 degrees Fahrenheit is equal to** -40 degrees Celsius.**__
 
• **-574.25 degrees** is the temperature that shows the same measurement in Kelvin and Fahrenheit scales.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of which neighbouring country of India overturned the rulings of the courts of the said country in connection with a sportswear deal involving the famous US basketball player Michael Jordan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China.**__

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of China**__ overturned the rulings of the courts in connection with a sportswear deal involving the famous US basketball player** Michael Jordan.**
 
• China’s Supreme People’s Court overturned earlier rulings in favour of** Qiaodan Sports** using the characters Jordan’s Chinese name, although it upheld a ruling allowing the firm to use the Romanized version **“Qiaodan”.**
 
• The Supreme Court decision overturns two previous verdicts in favour of the Chinese firm.
 
• This judgement concluded the eight-year legal battle between Michael Jordan and the Chinese sportswear firm that **illegally used his name.**
 
• The company had built its business around Jordan's Chinese name and famous jersey number **“23” without his permission.**
 
• Jordan won the right to his name in Chinese characters in **2016,** but the Supreme Court upheld the firm's right to use its trademark "Qiaodan" in Romanised English.

questions.question: In which year did the British gain control of Delhi after defeating the Marathas?
questions.solution:

• The British troops were under the leadership of **General Lake**, and Marathas of Scindia’s army were under **General Louis Bourquin.**
 
• The battle was fought at **Patparganj** across the Yamuna River.
 
• The British gained control of Delhi after defeating the Marathas in **1803.__**
 
• Even though the British captured Delhi the capital of British India was at **Calcutta.**
 
• The Mughal emperor was allowed to continue living in the palace complex in the Red Fort.
 
• The modern city(present Delhi) developed only after 1911 when Delhi became the capital of British India.
 
• The period from 1830 to 1857 referred to as the period of the **Delhi renaissance.**

questions.question: The Himalayas consist of ______ main parallel ranges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Himalaya is the **youngest fold mountain **range in the world.
 
• The word Himalaya means "**the abode of snow**".
 
• The Himalaya is mostly formed of sedimentary rocks.
 
• The Himalayas consist of **three**__ main parallel ranges, namely:
 
 
• The greater Himalayas.
 
• The lesser Himalayas.
 
• The outer Himalayas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The northernmost range of the Himalaya is known as the **Great Himalayas.**

 
 
• It is also called Himadri.
 
• Himadri is the backbone of the Himalaya.
 
• It is the most continuous range consisting of the loftiest peaks with an average height of 6,000 metres.
 
• It contains all the prominent Himalayan peaks like Mount Everest, Annapoorna, Nandadevi, etc.
 
 
 
• The **Lesser Himalayas **is the mountain range that lies between Himadri and Siwalik.
 
 
• It is also called Himachal.
 
• It is mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.
 
• The altitude varies between 3,700 and 4,500 metres and the average width is 50 Km.
 
• Pir Panjal is the largest range in Himachal.
 
• This region is well known for its hill stations.
 
 
 
• The outermost range of the Himalayas is called the **Shiwalik**(Outer Himalayas.)
 
 
• It extends over a width of 10-50 Km and has an altitude varying between 900 and 1100 metres.
 
• The word Shiwalik literally means "tresses of Shiva".
 
• Shiwalik is parallel to the Ganga plain.

questions.question: At which of the following places did Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri pass away?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tashkent**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri is the prime minister who signed on Tashkent agreement**__.
 
• Tashkent is the capital city of Uzbekistan.
 
• The Tashkent Declaration was a peace agreement between India and Pakistan to resolve the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1965.**
 
• It was signed between **Lal Bahadur Shastri and the then-President of Pakistan Muhammad Ayub Khan** on 10th January 1966.
 
• He died in **Tashkent **on the same day after the Tashkent Declaration (10th January 1966).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri **was the second Prime minister of India.

 
 
• He served as the Prime minister of India from 1964 to 1965.
 
• He is popularly called **"man of peace**".
 
• He was the Prime Minister of India during the **Indo-Pak war in 1965.**
 
• His birthday also falls on **2ⁿd October** along with Mahatma Gandhi's birthday.
 
• The famous slogan "**Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan**" was raised by Lal Bahadur Shastri.
 
• He is the first prime minister to **die abroad.**
 
• He was honoured with the **Bharat Ratna in 1966.**
 
• He was the first person to receive Bharat Ratna posthumously.
 
• The resting place of Lal Bahadur Shastri is called **Vijayghat.**

questions.question: How many hydrogen atoms are there in a molecule of acetylene?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Acetylene** is the chemical compound with the chemical formula C₂H₂.
 
• There are** 2 hydrogen atoms **__present in an acetylene molecule.
 
• Acetylene is the **first stable member** of the alkyne series.
 
• Acetylene is also called **ethyne.**
 
• Acetylene is unsaturated in nature due to the presence of a **triple bond** between two carbon atoms.
 
• Acetylene was discovered by **Edmund Davy** in 1836.
 
• It is widely used as a fuel and a chemical building block.
 
• Acetylene is used for** arc welding** purposes in the form of oxyacetylene flame obtained by mixing acetylene with oxygen gas.

questions.question: Who among the following had the title of ‘Abla Baba’ (friend of the poor) of the Deccan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibrahim Adil Shah II.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ibrahim Adil Shah II__ **was king of the Bijapur Sultanate.
 
• He was a member of the **Adil Shahi dynasty.**
 
• He had the title of ‘**Abla Baba**’ (friend of the poor) of the Deccan.
 
• He had a title called ‘**Jagadguru Badshah**’
 
• Adil Shahi dynasty had its greatest period Under his reign.
 
• He ruled the dynasty from **1580 to 1626.**
 
• He was an expert in Indian music and author of a book on this subject, Nauras-nama.
 
• He renovated **Dutta temples** in his fort and encouraged pooja rituals.
 
• He worked for the cultural harmony of Hindu-Muslim.
 
• He wrote a book called ‘**Kitab-e-Navaras**’ and tried to make music popular among Muslims.
 
• ‘**Ibrahim Rauza**’ which is famous for its architecture was built by Ibrahim Adil Shah II.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ali Adil Shah I **was the fifth Sultan of Bijapur Sultanate.

 
 
• He established diplomatic relations with the Mughal Emperor Akbar and envoys were exchanged.
 
 
 
• **Mir Jumla II **was a prominent subahdar of Bengal under Aurangzeb.
 
 
• He invaded the Ahom kingdom in January 1662.
 
 
 
• **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** was the fourth ruler of the kingdom of Golconda.
 
 
• He was the first of the Qutb Shahi dynasty to use the title "Sultan".
